questions.question:
**In the given sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

Freedom of expression meaning the right to express one’s own convictions and beliefs.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is - **meaning the right.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The simple present tense is used when an action is happening right now, **to state or ask about things in general, **or when it happens regularly or unceasingly.
 
• The structure is given below:
 
 
• Subject + V1 + object.
 
 
 
• The verb will take 's/es' if the given noun/pronoun (3rd person) is singular.
 
• Example:
 
 
• *​He plays badminton daily.*
 
 
 
• In the given part of the sentence, we need a simple present verb tense as a general statement has been given here.
 
• Since 'freedom' is a singular noun, the singular verb i.e., 'means' will be used.

Correct Sentence__: *Freedom of expression **means **the right to express one’s own convictions and beliefs.*

* *​​​​ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** 

 
• Certain verbs used only in the simple present tense are given below:

 
 
• ​See, think, know, possess, like, want, desire, hate, seem, imagine, etc.
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *​My brother is owning a car. (incorrect)*
 
• *​My brother owns a car. (correct)*

questions.question:
**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

Firecrackers have seized by the government went off while being defused on the banks of the river Ganga, in a town in West Bengal.

options.text: on the banks of the river Ganga
in a town in West Bengal
Firecrackers have seized by the government

questions.solution:
The correct answer is- **Firecrackers have seized by the government​.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The present perfect tense is a verb tense that shows an action or state that either occurred at an indefinite time in the past or began in the past and continued to the present time.
 
• The structure is given below:
 
 
• Subject + has/have + V3 + object. (active voice)
 
• Object + has/have + been + V3 + subject. (passive voice)
 
 
 
• ​Example:
 
 
• *​He has played some matches for the Indian Cricket team. (active voice)*
 
• *Some matches have been played by him for the Indian Cricket team. (passive voice)*
 
 
 
• In the given blank, we need to follow the structure in the passive voice form as reflected by the usage of the preposition 'by'.
 
• Hence according to the rule given above, 'have been seized' is the most appropriate choice.

 

Correct Sentence__: *Firecrackers **have been seized** by the government went off while being defused on the banks of the river Ganga, in a town in West Bengal.*

questions.question:
**Spot the error in the given sentence and select the correct sentence from the options given.**

Is Savita is joining us for lunch today?

options.text: Is Savita joining us for lunch today?
Savita is joined us for lunch today?

Are Savita joining us for lunch today?

questions.solution:

__
 
• Among the given sentence the correctly structured sentence is **'Is Savita joining us for lunch today?'.**
 
• This sentence is an example of **present continuous tense** which starts with** a helping verb.**
 
• The structure of these kinds of sentences is: **Is/Am/Are + Subject + V1 + ing + Object?**
 
 
• *Example: **Are** **we going **to the picnic this evening?*
 
 
 
• Thus, the correct answer is** Option 1.**

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *Is Savita **joining** us for lunch today?*

questions.question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

More than 40 percent of the world’s population lives in regions where water has becoming increasingly scarce.

options.text: More than 40 percent of the world’s population

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence contains an **error in option 1**: "has becoming increasingly scarce".
 
• The** problem lies** in the **verb tense.**
 
• **In English,** the **present perfect tense** is** formed by** using "has" or "have" followed by a past participle (in most cases, a verb ending in -ed).
 
• The verb **"become" **should be used in its past participle form, "become", not "becoming".
 
• The phrase should be corrected to** "has become increasingly scarce".**

Therefore, the **correct sentence** is:* "More than 40 percent of the world’s population lives in regions where water has become increasingly scarce."*

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **to struggled with**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• Subject + has/have + V3 + object. (active voice)
 
• Object + has/have + been + V3 + subject. (passive voice)
 
 
 
• ​Example:
 
 
• *​He has played some matches for the Indian Cricket team. (active voice)*
 
• *Some matches have been played by him for the Indian Cricket team. (passive voice)*
 
 
 
• In the given sentence, we need to follow the structure in the active voice form.
 
• Since the given sentence talks about the action that continues till the present time, 'has struggled' is the most appropriate choice of the verb form instead of '**has to struggled**' in the part given in the** 4th option.**
 
• Thus we are left with the 4th option as the only correct choice.

 

Correct Sentence__: *The country has **struggled **with the problems of child labour.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/51867102c7c2f369f6e29d2efe025e3b3367c68261ec20262828d84ca5c8f854.png] **__Hinglish__**

__
 
• Present perfect tense एक क्रिया काल है जो एक क्रिया या अवस्था को दर्शाता है जो या तो अतीत में अनिश्चित समय पर घटित होता है या अतीत में शुरू होता है और वर्तमान समय तक जारी रहता है।
 
• संरचना नीचे दी गई है:
 
 
• Subject + has/have + V3 + object. (active voice)
 
• Object + has/have + been + V3 + subject. (passive voice)
 
 
 
• उदाहरण:
 
 
• *​He has played some matches for the Indian Cricket team. (active voice)*
 
• *Some matches have been played by him for the Indian Cricket team. (passive voice)*
 
 
 
• दिए गए वाक्य में, हमें active voice रूप में संरचना का पालन करने की आवश्यकता है।
 
• कार्रवाई है कि वर्तमान समय तक जारी रहता है के बारे में दिए गए वाक्य वार्ता के बाद से, ''has struggled' के बजाय 4 विकल्प में दिए गए हिस्से में 'has to struggled' के क्रिया रूप का सबसे उपयुक्त विकल्प है।
 
• **इस प्रकार , उत्तर 4 विकल्प है**

सही वाक्य:__ *The country has struggled with the problems of child labour.*

questions.question:
In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains a grammatical error.

Where did you kept the sack of wheat that I bought from the market?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Option 1'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sentence is in "**Past Indefinite Tense",** and it's an "**interrogative sentence"**.
 
• In such sentences, we always use "**did &** **verb 1st form"**.
 
• So, using verb 2nd form *i.e. **kept**, *is **inappropriate **here.

We should use **'Where did you keep', **instead of **'Where did you kept'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

The basic rule for Past Indefinite Tense (Interrogative Sentence):-

 
• Wh family + did + subject + verb 1st form + object?
 
 
• Why **did **you **go **there? not (went there)
 
• Where **did **you **meet **him yesterday?
 
• How **did **you **solve** that sum?
 
 

Hence, the correct sentence is *"**Where did you keep** the sack of wheat that I bought from the market"?*

questions.question:
**In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error**

According to environment activists, the demolition of unauthorized apartment complexes are became a lesson for land encroachers.

options.text: the demolition of unauthorized apartment complexes

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'are became'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The erroneous Part **'are became'** should be **'has become'. **
 
• The given sentence has** two errors.** Here, **the present perfect tense** should be used because this tense is used with work started in the part and at present just finished. 
 
• First, **'has' **should be used because **the main subject** of the given sentence is **'the demolition'. **
 
• And the second error **'became'** should be **'become' **because with **'has**' auxiliary verb **'past participle form' **should be used. 
 
• Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 1. 

 ​**

**Correct Answer:__** *According to environment activists, the demolition of unauthorized apartment complexes **has become** a lesson for land encroachers. * 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The other usage of Present Perfect Tense:
 
 
• Time Expression: If time expression is mentioned at the last of a sentence or a word like since, for, how long, whole, all, throughout, all along is mentioned then the sentence should be in present perfect. 

 
 
• *Example: I have worked here since I graduated from school. *

questions.question:
**In the sentence identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

Mani Kaul begun his career as an actor and a director of short films before doing his debut feature film, ‘Uski Roti.’

options.text: begun his career as an actor

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **begun his career as an actor​.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The simple past tense is used when we talk about things that happened or existed before now.
 
• The structure is given below:
 
 
• Subject + V2 + object. (Active Voice)
 
• Object + was/were + V3 + by + subject. (Passive Voice)
 
 
 
• Example:
 
 
• *​He won the car race. (active voice)*
 
• *The car race was won by him. (passive voice)*
 
 
 
• Since the sentence follows the active voice structure, the 2nd form of the verb i.e. began will be used instead of 'begun' in part given in the 2nd option.

 

Correct Sentence__:* **Mani Kaul **began **his career as an actor and a director of short films before doing his debut feature film, ‘Uski Roti.’*
